headline: GOLD FALLS TO TWO-MONTH LOW AT $4,380 AS US STRIKES ON IRAN STOKE INFLATION FEARS
snippet: Gold dropped to its lowest level since late March at $4,380/oz on May 28 as fresh U.S. strikes on Iran stoked inflation fears and pushed the dollar to a one-week high, eroding safe-haven demand from buyers of other currencies. Spot gold was down 1.7% and briefly breached $4,396 before stabilising.

headline: $4,400 GOLD FUELS MINING M&A SCALE RACE — Analysts See No End to 2026 Consolidation Wave
snippet: With gold sustaining above $4,400 and miners generating robust free cash flow, mid-tier and senior producers are openly racing to acquire ounces through M&A — analysts say no slowdown is in sight after a string of multi-billion dollar combinations already closed in 2026, including the Equinox-Orla and Regis-Vault deals.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.40/LB: AI Data Center Boom Meets Middle East Sulfur Supply Squeeze
snippet: Copper futures held at $6.40/lb on May 27 as sustained strength in AI-linked tech stocks lifted industrial demand expectations, while concerns about Middle East disruptions to sulfuric acid supply chains — nearly half of which originates from Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE — added additional price support.

headline: Bayhorse Silver Completes Underground Drill Prep — 2,000m Program Starts June 1
snippet: Bayhorse Silver has finished underground drill preparations at its Oregon silver mine, with a minimum 13-hole, 2,000-metre program set to commence June 1 targeting the CR-2 IP anomaly and easterly IP zones designed to expand beyond the existing 6.3 million oz NI 43-101 inferred silver resource.

headline: Magna Mining Posts $6M Positive Q1 Cash Margin, Earns Conditional Promotion to TSX
snippet: Magna Mining (TSXV: NICU) posted a $6.0 million positive cash margin at its McCreedy West copper-precious metals-nickel mine in Q1 2026, processing 82,296 tonnes at 3.38% CuEq, and received conditional approval to graduate from the TSXV to the TSX main board pending final requirements by July 29.

headline: Newmont vs. SSR Mining: Which Gold Stock Is a Better Buy at $4,400 Gold?
snippet: A Motley Fool analyst makes the case for SSR Mining over sector heavyweight Newmont at current gold prices, arguing the smaller producer offers faster production growth and greater upside leverage in a $4,400+ gold environment where valuation gaps between majors and mid-tiers remain unusually wide.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Surges 159% in 2026 — But Mine-to-Magnet Execution Risk Is Very Real
snippet: USA Rare Earth's Round Top deposit and Oklahoma magnet factory could make it the U.S.'s first vertically integrated rare earth producer, but the stock's 159% 2026 surge reflects both genuine strategic value and the kind of pre-revenue hype that has burned retail investors before.

headline: GoldMining Turns First Drill at Yarumalito Gold-Copper Project in Colombia's Mid Cauca Belt
snippet: GoldMining Inc. mobilized a diamond core drill for a 1,200-metre program at its 100%-owned Yarumalito project in Colombia's prolific Mid Cauca gold-copper belt on May 26, testing high-priority targets refined through comprehensive relogging of historical drill core at a belt that hosts several multi-million-ounce deposits.

headline: SULFURIC ACID CRUNCH HAMMERS BATTERY METAL COSTS — Nickel, Lithium Producers Squeezed as Hormuz Closes
snippet: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence data shows sulfur prices have surged more than 50% since the start of the Iran war, with spot sulfuric acid prices in Indonesia and Chile climbing above $380 and $440 per tonne — now representing 42% of HPAL nickel processing costs, up from 26%, and squeezing margins across lithium, cobalt, and rare earth refining globally.
